case.pattern_description: The pattern consists of four rapid online purchases completed within thirty to forty minutes, each structured just below a $500 authorization threshold. This activity affects individual cardholders via unauthorized online transactions initiated from novel devices, including one routing through a transparent proxy. The pattern was identified by analyzing the card timeline burst shape and matching it to closed bank cases CC-3748, CC-3841, and CC-3907.

case.summary: Between 2016-11-21 20:00 and 2016-11-21 20:30, card C07297-K1 was used for four unauthorized online transactions totaling $1,906.07, each priced just under a $500 threshold. The cardholder reported transaction 3476682 as fraudulent, denied making any of the purchases, and confirmed the physical card remained in their possession. It was assumed that the pattern aligns with identical confirmed fraud cases CC-3748, CC-3841, CC-3907, CC-4086, and CC-4124. Card C07297-K1 has been blocked and recommended for reissue, and a suspicious activity report is filed under rules R2 and R9.

sar.narrative: This suspicious activity report concerns unauthorized online card transactions associated with customer C07297 on card account C07297-K1. Between 2016-11-21 20:00 and 2016-11-21 20:30, four transactions totaling $1,906.07 were processed in rapid succession: transaction 3476602 for $478.95, transaction 3476633 for $456.96, transaction 3476665 for $488.04, and transaction 3476682 for $482.12. The online purchases originated from device profiles Trident/7.0 | Windows 7 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080 and iOS Device | iOS 11.2.1 | mobile safari 11.0 | 2208x1242, with one device operating behind a transparent proxy. On 2016-11-22, customer C07297 submitted a report disputing transaction 3476682. When contacted, the cardholder confirmed that they still possessed the physical card and denied initiating any of the four purchases. The activity exhibits deliberate velocity and structured pricing just below a $500 authorization threshold to avoid triggering standard velocity controls. This burst shape matches documented fraud signatures previously confirmed in cases CC-4124, CC-4086, CC-3907, CC-3841, and CC-3748. In accordance with policy rules R2 and R9, card C07297-K1 has been blocked and submitted for reissue, and the total fraudulent exposure of $1,906.07 is reported.
